source.title: Temperature Balancing, Layer-wise Weight Analysis, and Neural Network Training
source.authors: Ye-Fan Zhou; Tian-Yu Pang; Keqin Liu; Charles H. Martin; Michael W. Mahoney; Yao-Qing Yang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and tables.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks and reports test accuracy, spectral statistics, and gradient norms, but does not report training classification error or test the claim versions about reaching near-zero training error, shortcuts, initialization, or learning-rate stability.
record.gate_note: No rows: the reported CIFAR experiments compare test accuracy, not training classification error. Gradient norms and weight-spectrum analyses do not measure the claimed training-error outcome. Accuracy values used to compare TempBalance with other methods are outside the claim’s measure.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates TempBalance through test performance, weight spectra, and gradient norms. It reports no training classification error, teacher–student local-minimum frequencies, controlled shortcut or initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch-normalization comparisons. Appendix F's transient gradient explosion does not establish V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that TempBalance uses a heavy-tail spectral metric to balance layer-wise learning rates and improve test performance in their evaluated settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a layer-wise learning-rate schedule and compares test performance; it does not evaluate the claim’s training-error outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies across architecture, dataset, width, learning-rate settings, and learning-rate assignment choices; these do not establish the claim’s training-error measure.

fits_no_version.finding: TempBalance improves test accuracy relative to cosine-annealed SGD across the main classification settings; additional experiments report improved detection mAP and language-model test perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise learning-rate assignment guided by weight-spectrum heavy-tail estimates can improve generalization in the evaluated settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix F reports gradient explosion confined to the first epoch and no observed gradient vanishing in ResNet18 on CIFAR100. Delaying TempBalance until epochs 2, 5, or 10 preserves comparable test performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TempBalance's generalization benefit in this setting does not depend on addressing the initial gradient explosion.

record.problems: For the claim’s outcome, the paper reports no training classification error measurements. Its principal results concern test accuracy and weight-spectrum metrics; many plotted results are not numerically transcribed in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows meet the required measure. The study reports test accuracy comparisons in Sections 4.2–4.3 and appendices, not training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error on clean or corrupted labels, including its dependence on model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths change, including the benefit of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and training with special initialization or Fixup.
Effects of activation-matched, orthogonal, or Gaussian initialization on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Loss recovery above an initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below or above the threshold.
Effects of batch normalization on learning speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for V1–V6. Varying initial learning rate is not varying weight initialization, and observing a transient gradient spike without loss recovery or a measured stability threshold does not test V5. The record's relation='tests' should be corrected; its T6 assignment is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large randomly initialized convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error, including with corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes on training error.
Whether student width relative to teacher width changes spurious-minimum frequency in the stated two-layer ReLU teacher-student setting.
Whether plain-network depth raises training error relative to residual networks, and whether special initialization or Fixup permits deep training without shortcuts or normalization.
Whether activation-matched or orthogonal initialization changes training speed or trainable depth, including 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Whether above-stability learning rates cause a loss rise and recovery, how sharpness behaves during full-batch training, and whether runs diverge below the threshold.
Whether batch normalization changes accuracy learning speed or tolerated learning rates, and whether Fixup permits residual networks to train without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
